questions.stem: Bones of the upper (thoracic) limb, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: a is the clavicle, b the humerus, c the scapula (seen through the thorax), d the radius (lateral, thumb side) and e the ulna (medial).

questions.stem: Bones of the upper (thoracic) limb, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: f points to the carpus, g to the metacarpals and h to the phalanges. The radius (d) lies on the thumb side, the ulna (e) on the little-finger side.

questions.stem: Shoulder girdle, superior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: a is the scapula (acromion and spine seen from above), b the first rib, c the body of a thoracic vertebra, d the clavicle and f the manubrium of the sternum.

questions.stem: Clavicle, inferior view. Which statements are correct?
options: The extremity bearing a and c is the acromial (lateral) end
b marks the costal tuberosity, on the medial part
b marks the groove of the subclavius muscle
questions.explanation: The flattened lateral end carries the conoid tubercle (a) and trapezoid line (c); the costal tuberosity (b) lies medially. The subclavius groove runs along the middle of the inferior surface, not at the end.

questions.stem: Scapula, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: c is the coracoid process (d is the glenoid cavity), and f is the lateral (axillary) border; the medial border is g, on the opposite side.

questions.stem: Scapula, posterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: The spine (j) separates the supraspinous (i) and infraspinous (k) fossae. g is the medial (spinal) border; the lateral border is f, running down from the glenoid cavity.

questions.stem: Scapula, lateral view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: In lateral view the glenoid cavity (c) faces the viewer, overhung by the acromion (a) behind and the coracoid process (b) in front; d is the lateral (axillary) border ending at the inferior angle (e).

questions.stem: Humerus, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: c is the anatomical neck, the narrow groove bordering the head; the surgical neck (f) is lower, below the tubercles.

questions.stem: Humerus, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: g is the deltoid tuberosity on the lateral side of the shaft. d is the lesser tubercle, seen only anteriorly; the greater tubercle (a) is lateral and visible on both views.

questions.stem: Distal humerus, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: j is the coronoid fossa (anterior, above the trochlea); the olecranon fossa (k) is posterior. m is the capitulum (lateral, rounded), n the trochlea.

questions.stem: Distal humerus, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: k is the olecranon fossa on the posterior surface. The radial fossa (above the capitulum, anteriorly) is not labelled here.

questions.stem: Radius (left) and ulna, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
options: k → ulnar notch of the radius
l → styloid process of the radius
questions.explanation: j is the radial tuberosity (insertion of biceps brachii), just below the radial head (i). k is the ulnar notch on the medial side of the distal radius; l its lateral styloid process.

questions.stem: Ulna, anterior and lateral views. Which matches are correct?
options: g → styloid process of the ulna
questions.explanation: b is the trochlear notch (between olecranon and coronoid process) and d the radial notch on the lateral side of the coronoid process. g is the head of the ulna; the styloid process is h.

questions.stem: Ulna, lateral view. What does label h point to?
questions.explanation: h is the small styloid process projecting below the head of the ulna (g).

questions.stem: Carpal bones, palmar view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: Proximal row, lateral to medial: scaphoid (1), lunate (4), triquetrum (5), pisiform (6). Distal row: trapezium (2), trapezoid (3), capitate (8), hamate (7).

questions.stem: Carpal bones, palmar view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. The distal row from lateral to medial is trapezium (2), trapezoid (3), capitate (8), hamate (7); the triquetrum (5) is in the proximal row.

questions.stem: Carpal bones, dorsal view. Which carpal bone has no number in this view?
questions.explanation: The pisiform (6) sits on the palmar surface of the triquetrum, so it is hidden in dorsal view; the numbering skips 6.

questions.stem: Skeleton of the hand, palmar view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: 9 marks the five metacarpals and 10 the phalanges; 11 the sesamoid bones at the thumb's metacarpophalangeal joint. 1 is the scaphoid.
